# 2 Baruch Chapter 36 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 36 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 36:3 — "lowly and humble"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lowly and-humble" | Preserves both Syriac adjectives |
| LOGOS | "lowly and humble" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "low and humble" | Minor synonym |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "lowly and humble" (EMET/LOGOS). "Lowly" is more evocative than "low" in this context — the vine's lowly status is its defining characteristic against the lofty cedars.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Minor difference.

---

## 36:5 — "head of the cedars / great head-cedar"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-head-of-the-cedars" | Literal: Syriac risha d-arze = head/chief of the cedars |
| LOGOS | "the head of the cedars" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "the great head-cedar" | Interprets as a single chief tree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS "the head of the cedars." This refers to the leading cedar, which in the vision represents the final great empire (Rome). The phrase should remain as a construct, not be collapsed to "head-cedar."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 36:9 — "saw this and arose / woke up"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-saw this and-I-arose" | Two verbs: saw + arose |
| LOGOS | "I saw this and I arose" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "I woke up" | Simplifies to single verb |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS "I saw this and I arose." The two verbs are in the Syriac; the act of seeing and then arising are distinct. PNEUMA's "woke up" collapses this.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
